### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8939315c05db979e2efa3d9e7bb01bad1ae9e51` — the merge of head `7946ad1a22ad11165622f96a79a68aa39924be59` into base `68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8939315c05db979e2efa3d9e7bb01bad1ae9e51 && git checkout c8939315c05db979e2efa3d9e7bb01bad1ae9e51
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a 7946ad1a22ad11165622f96a79a68aa39924be59 && git checkout -B drift-repro 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a && git merge --no-ff 7946ad1a22ad11165622f96a79a68aa39924be59

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 68a090fb97fe49c685d303d13001b680c50f2f2a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7946ad1a22ad11165622f96a79a68aa39924be59`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-formula-hop-stored-metadata-body.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.stored-metadata-body-hop.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-metadata-body-family.pin.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/master-detail.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-formula-one-hop.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/stored-metadata-body-objects.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.data-door-stored-metadata-redaction.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, .changeset/24316-formula-hop-family-refusal.md (prose face, judged under ②)

Security card: this record keeps to category and position. It names symbols, files, reader classes and dispositions only; no request string, no path into a stored body, no value.

Read-only shape held: the net diff (`ec749fbb44..7946ad1a22`, 7 files, +461/-2), the card and its four comments, the PR body and file list, and the 40 check-runs on the head (34 success, 6 skipped conditional or opt-in jobs, 0 failures; Check Changeset, Lint · repo & tooling gates and Governed Surface Queue Guard among the green). Nothing built, run or re-run. The dev's `os-dev-report` 6250893952 and the PR's reach table were read as claims; every judgment below is from the cited code.

### ① Derived judgments

**The guard and its placement — right.** `resolveOneHopRelated` (`engine.ts:10090`) is the one loader; its only callers are `resolveFormulaRelated` (`engine.ts:6252`, authority `caller`) and `resolvePredicateRelated` (`engine.ts:10057`, authority `predicate`), confirmed by a repository-wide grep. The new branch (`engine.ts:10132`) sits first in the per-reference loop: the only statement before it is the pure `referenceTargetOf(fields[fk])`, so a target the family predicate (`isStoredMetadataBodyObject`, `@objectstack/spec/kernel`, the one membership set) names is never the subject of any `find`, under either authority, before any id set is built. The engine test's `familyReads()` counter pins "never issued" for every exit it drives. Both authorities: the branch precedes the `authority` split at `engine.ts:10227`, so a SYSTEM caller is refused as a member is (pinned for `find`, `serveFormulaField` and the rule).

**Hops no longer read — right, both authorities.** (a) The caller-authority formula hop, on every path that reaches `resolveFormulaRelated`: `find` (`engine.ts:14081`, which is also what a hook body's `ctx.api.object(...)` read of a carrier reaches, the sandbox seam refusing only the family object itself, `body-runner.ts:366/532`), `findOne` (`engine.ts:14370`), the insert and update responses (`engine.ts:16113`, `17913`), and `serveFormulaField` (`engine.ts:6303`, the seam `ctx.title()` reads through). (b) The SYSTEM-authority validation-rule hop (`resolvePredicateRelated`, hydrated `script` / `cross_field` conditions, nested branches included).

**What each read surface now answers — right, and the 'unreadable' shape discloses nothing about the row.** The binding is `{ byId: empty, blocked: true }`, which the per-row closure turns into `{ object, unavailable: 'unreadable' }` (`engine.ts:10270`), byte-identical to the binding a thrown read gets (`engine.ts:10257`) and to a row a bound caller's own read did not return (`engine.ts:10279`). A formula: `formulaHopScope` → `formulaHopRefusal` 'unreadable' (`engine.ts:2721`) → the field reads `null` and the fault sink logs at `warn` a sentence naming the columns, the reference field and the related object, never a value; a validation rule: `resolveTraversalScope` → `traversalRefusal` 'unreadable' (`rule-validator.ts:4271`) → no verdict, the write refused with the existing unevaluable shape (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `rule_violation`), the text naming the object and columns only. Before this change an administrator received the rule's own verdict over the unprojected body (a one-bit oracle per write); now no caller receives any verdict that depends on the row, so there is no oracle. The find, findOne and write-response answers carry `null` in the formula slot; the test's `servesNothing` asserts no placeholder reaches any of them, the fault text included.

**The lint — right.** `storedMetadataBodyReferencesOf` indexes an object's reference fields (lookup / master_detail / user / tree via `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`; `user`'s implied target is `sys_user`, never the family) whose carrier names a family table, read through `referenceCarrierOf` with the literal `.reference` in argument position for the #5017 scan. `refuseStoredMetadataBodyHop` runs at exactly the two sites that serve a hop: `check(...)` with `traversalHydration` (`validate-expressions.ts:2129`; the top-level `condition` at 2713 and the nested #22042 conditions) and `judgeFieldFormula` (2850). It fires only when `analyzeRelationshipTraversals` reports a traversal through an indexed field, so a bare read of the reference (the stored id) is untouched, as the lint test pins. The message is an `error` naming the reference, the table, and the columns read, with the prescription (read stored metadata through the metadata API, where the body is projected), no tracker number, no row content. Field-rule slots and option `visibleWhen` already refuse any read through a reference and `when` is never hydrated, so no third served site exists. The index is read lazily (second commit), so an unreadable carrier is still refused by the pass that owned that verdict.

**Which save doors run that pass — right, and the NOT MEASURED door settled in code.** The expression rule's registry entry declares `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow','action','hook','object']` and runs `runStackExpressionPasses(stack, { runtimeWriteType })` (`authoring-rules.ts:685-688`). `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` reach it through `runAuthoringRules` (`cli/src/commands/validate.ts:530`, `compile.ts:553`, `lint.ts:681`, `utils/artifact-packages.ts:308`). The object save door reaches it through `saveMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:22599`) → `runAuthoringGate` (7170) → `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` → `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (`lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:1039`), for draft and publish saves alike. The unmanaged package import (`importUnmanagedPackage`, `protocol.ts:28277`) writes every item through `saveMetaItem`, so it is gated. The managed install primitive (`installPackage`, `protocol.ts:31808`) parses `PackageInstallManifestSchema` and calls `registry.installPackage` directly: no authoring rule runs there, for this rule as for every other expression rule, and that is pre-existing. The engine guard holds whatever door admitted the carrier, so this is a loudness gap of the install door, not an exit; noted under ③.

**Non-family hops unchanged — right.** The branch keys on the family predicate alone; the engine test pins `other_out` served on the same carrier, the lint test pins a hop into an ordinary object and a bare id read producing no issue. The one asymmetry: the lint trims the carrier, the engine's `referenceTargetOf` does not. A whitespace-padded carrier naming the family passes the engine branch, but the registry knows no object by that padded name, so the loader's `find` throws and the binding is 'unreadable' with no family read issued. Not a leak; a nit.

**Reading the reference field's own stored id — unchanged.** A bare `record.fk` is a `bareFields` member of the traversal analysis (`relationship-traversal.ts:253`), never a hop; neither the engine nor the lint touches it.

**Is every exit to a family row covered — the loader, yes; two sibling hydrations outside the loader are not this card's position and are escalated under ③.** (i) `expandRelatedRecords` (`engine.ts:12917`): the engine's `expand` relationship hydration through a reference into a family target is an ordinary engine `find` on the target under the caller's own full gate (`security-plugin.ts:2618-2669`), and the generic data door projects the requested object only (`redactStoredMetadataRows(request.object, ...)`, `protocol.ts:14796`, `14942`); the door's expand gate (`protocol.ts:13425-13469`) refuses unknown, non-reference and targetless fields and nothing else. (ii) The master-detail `parent` root: `resolveMasterDetailParent` / `resolveMasterDetailParents` (`engine.ts:9762`, `9818`) bind the header from an elevated whole-row `findOne` / `find` after the caller's id-only door read, and `resolveMasterDetailRelation` (`master-detail.ts:220`) has no family check. Neither reaches `resolveOneHopRelated`, neither is named by the card, and neither is a row of the family pin. The PR's claim, "one guard covers every exit that reaches the loader", is exact as written.

**The family pin — right.** `FAMILY_SURFACES` 23 → 26 (8 original + 15 of #21207 + 3 here, counted); the header enumerates the two new per-package pins; each new row names its owning pin and the exits it covers match the engine test's drives.

### ② Semver level

Right. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, carries the `!` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the PR body carries the same line, its trailing parenthetical read as reasoning by `readArmToken` (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`), the arm being the first token of the first parenthetical. `no` is the truthful value: nothing widens (a new refusal narrows the accept set; the engine narrows the served set). ADR-0087's ratified launch-window section (amended 2026-09-13, #18003) states the level: pre-GA, a break ships `minor` carrying the banner and its disposition, an npm `major` being a planned act, and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses a `major`; the fixed group is at `18.0.0-next.3`. The disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest on the facts the changeset states: no spec key, export, option or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the "What to do" paragraph is an authoring repair (remove the read; the id read is unchanged), not a mechanical FROM → TO rewrite, and the gate (green on this head) did not accept it on a detector miss but because the claim is true. One changeset file for two packages where the claim said "one changeset per package touched": a changesets entry may bump several packages and both receive the same body; acceptable.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Disclosure line — kept.** PR body, changeset, the card's four comments, every code comment and every test name describe category and position: which reader classes were served before the fix, with counts, and which disposition each surface now has. No request string, no value. The test fixtures use synthetic placeholders in the shape the family pin already publishes on `main` (`stored-metadata-body-family.pin.test.ts:153-164`), and the column names the tests read are the spec's own published constants. The lint message embeds only the prescription's public metadata-API path. Not a FAIL finding.

**Deviations — each judged.**
- `validate-expressions.test.ts` (outside the claim list): the #5017 receiver meta-test excuses three new locals, `storedMetadataBodyReferenceIndex`, `familyRefs`, `traversals`, all Maps whose keys are Map / Set methods; the metadata keys the index is built from (`type`, `reference`) are read off the tabled `def` receiver from `fieldEntries`. No metadata receiver is masked. Right, and reported as the claim required.
- No `packages/formula` edit: the claim admitted that package only if the admission were decided there; the lint already holds the object's reference fields and reuses formula's `analyzeRelationshipTraversals`. Right.
- Reusing 'unreadable' rather than a new reason kind: right for a security card. The runtime answer is the one shape that says nothing about whether the row exists, is forbidden, or is a family row; the loud prescription is at every author-time door that runs the pass; adding a reason kind would touch `rule-validator.ts`, outside the claim.
- Commit trailers: the commits carry the model-free `Claude-Session` / `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair AGENTS.md prescribes; the harness reminder is not the repo's rule. Right.
- No `subscribe_pr_activity`, worktree handling: process notes, no contract effect.

**Open questions — answered.**
- Hop granularity, whole table (A, landed) vs body / hash columns (B): A. The family refuses the whole table at every other app-authored reach (hook body reads, flow writes), the card forbids a second projection, a column list would be a second definition of what leaks, and the stored id stays readable. Nothing real is lost: a grep of the repository's metadata finds no reference into the family.
- Runtime wording (A, landed): A for this card. B is a wording follow-up in `rule-validator.ts` and `formulaHopRefusal` with no security content; it may be filed as a devx note, not required here.

**Out-of-scope findings — judged, two escalated.** Not filed by this review (no GitHub writes); the owning `domain:engine` seat files them, category and position only.
- Package install door (dev: NOT MEASURED): settled in code above. The managed `installPackage` primitive runs no authoring rule (pre-existing for every expression rule; an artifact reaches it after `os build` ran the same pass); the unmanaged import goes through `saveMetaItem`. The engine guard holds at both. No card needed on this position; a general note that the managed install primitive runs no authoring rule may be filed as a devx card.
- Master-detail `parent` root (dev: measured unbound for a family master, noted only): ESCALATE. The binding path (`resolveMasterDetailParent`, elevated whole-row header read, `resolveMasterDetailRelation` without a family check) shows no mechanism for the measured refusal in the cited code, and this PR's lint refusal covers `record.fk.column` hops and not a `parent.column` read in a field-rule slot or validation. Its own `[security]` card, measurement first, same family, same disclosure line.
- `expand` relationship hydration (found in this review, not by the dev): ESCALATE. `expandRelatedRecords` reads a family target by an ordinary engine `find` under the caller's own gate and the generic data door projects the requested object only; reach is bounded by the same reader classes this card's before-column names (readers whose own read of the family returns a row). Not the one-hop loader, not in the family pin. Its own `[security]` card, measurement first.

Neither escalation is a defect of this PR: the card's position is the one-hop loader and the lint's one-hop admission, both closed here with no second projection, no `packages/spec` edit, no new error code and no change to the doors' projection or the reader-context seam, as the claim required.
